title: Augmented cycle comparison extending a prescribed incoming boundary map
statement:
Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $F:A\to B$ be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits. Let $K,L$ be cochain complexes indexed by $\mathbb Z$, let $u:F(K)\to L$ be a complex map, and let $I,J$ be bicomplexes with horizontal index $\mathbb Z$ and resolution index $\mathbb N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $S_K=\operatorname{single}_0(K)$ and $S_L=\operatorname{single}_0(L)$, and let $e_I:S_K\to I$, $e_J:S_L\to J$ be bicomplex augmentations. For every horizontal degree $r$, put $\rho_K^r=\operatorname{singleObjXSelf}:S_K^{r,0}\xrightarrow{\sim}K^r$, define $\rho_L^r$ similarly, and put $\varepsilon_I^r=(e_I^r)^0(\rho_K^r)^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_J^r=(e_J^r)^0(\rho_L^r)^{-1}$. Write $G$ for applying $F$ to resolution complexes, $B_I^p=\operatorname{Im}(d_I^{p-1,p})$, and $\iota_{Z,J}^p:Z^p(J)\to J^p$ for the cycle inclusion. Injectivity below means injectivity in $B$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Fix $p\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose the induced augmentation maps on the cycle, incoming boundary and homology columns in degree $p$ are quasi-isomorphisms, both for $I$ and for $J$, and the corresponding three columns of $J$ are termwise injective. Let $b:G(B_I^p)\to B_J^p$ be a complex map satisfying $b^0F((\operatorname{factorThruImage}d_I^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_I^{p-1})=(\operatorname{factorThruImage}d_J^{p-1,p})^0\varepsilon_J^{p-1}u^{p-1}$. Then there is a complex map $y:G(Z^p(I))\to Z^p(J)$ such that
$\iota_{Z,J}^{p,0}y^0 F((\operatorname{cyclesMap}e_I,p)^0)=\varepsilon_J^p u^p F(\rho_K^p)F(\iota_{Z,S_K}^{p,0})$ and
$\iota_{Z,J}^p y G(\operatorname{toCycles}_I^{p-1,p})=\operatorname{image.\iota}(d_J^{p-1,p})bG(\operatorname{factorThruImage}(d_I^{p-1,p}))$.
No map on the object column or outgoing boundary column is asserted.

proof.text: Form $0\to B^p\to Z^p\to H^p\to0$ in each bicomplex. The boundary inclusion is the factor of image.\iota through cycles; its cokernel is homology. Evaluation is exact, so the sequence is degreewise short exact, and $G$ preserves it. The exact single-degree functor identifies the corresponding columns of $S_K,S_L$ with the single complexes on $B^p(K),Z^p(K),H^p(K)$ and the corresponding objects of $L$, naturally with respect to $u$ and the augmentations.

The supplied boundary augmentation square is the true square on $B^p(K)$: compose that square with $F(K^{p-1}\to B^p(K))$. Naturality of the augmentations gives exactly the assumed equation. This precomposition can be cancelled, since image factorization is epic in an abelian category and $F$ preserves epimorphisms.

The given homology augmentation quasi-isomorphisms, transported through the single-degree identifications and $F$, are resolutions of $F(H^p(K))$ and $H^p(L)$. The source augmentation is monomorphic: its degree-zero component identifies with the kernel of the first differential, and its other components have zero source. Lift the homology map induced by $u$ into the termwise injective target homology column along this monomorphic quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso]. Nonnegative indexing supplies the required bounded-below condition.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] to the boundary/cycles/homology short exact sequences, with prescribed endpoint maps $b$ and the homology lift. The target resolutions use the given augmented columns and their termwise injectivity; the source is an exact augmented row and need not have injective terms. The resulting middle map is $y$.

Compose its augmented cycle square with the target cycle inclusion. Naturality of the single-degree identifications gives the first formula as stated, on $S_K$ cycles in resolution degree zero. Compose its incoming square with the source factorThruImage and the target cycle inclusion; the factorization of the differential through its image and cycles gives the second formula. These operations do not choose any object-column map.
